ai_show_review.summary: Quirky acid‑test interview with rough jams, more doc than concert
ai_show_review.blurb: The tape blends a Ken Kesey interview with brief, free‑form jamming from the early Dead. Sound is decent for an acid‑test capture but lo‑fi and uneven. No conventional setlist – it’s a historical snapshot rather than a full show.
ai_show_review.review: On January 29, 1966 the Grateful Dead appeared at the Sound City Acid Test, a night that was as much about Ken Kesey’s psychedelic musings as it was about music. The best available recording (gd1966-01-29.sbd.bershaw.5411.shnf) offers a clearer field capture than most early acid‑test tapes, preserving snippets of the band’s early improvisations alongside Kesey’s interview. While the audio fidelity is modest and the flow feels more like an archival document than a concert, it provides a rare glimpse of the pre‑classic lineup with Pigpen on keys and vocals. A second audience‑style capture (gd1966-01-29.sbd.berger.99527.flac16) is even rougher; listeners note Jerry’s voice sounding “completely shot” on track 10, casting doubt on how much actual playing is present. Together the recordings are valuable for their historical context—showcasing the band’s embryonic stage and its ties to the Merry Pranksters—but they offer limited musical payoff for those seeking a traditional Dead performance.

best_recording.reason: Higher sound quality (good) and more complete capture of interview plus jam segments
